effects: Exactly `assets` USDe is pulled from the signer into the vault (safeTransferFrom in enter).
feUSDEv2 vault shares are minted to `onBehalf`. The amount is previewDeposit(assets), set by the share price after accrueInterest, and the call has no minimum.
The deposited USDe may be moved on into the liquidity adapter. That is vault-internal and changes nothing the signer holds.
formats.shown: Deposit 10 USDe for <onBehalf>, with the deposit amount, the share ticker feUSDEv2 and the share recipient as fields.

findings.title: deposit: the number of feUSDEv2 shares minted is not shown; the vault computes it and the call has no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. Case 0 minted 10 feUSDEv2 to the signer, and the screen shows only 'Share ticker: feUSDEv2'.
findings.fix: No calldata field holds the share amount. The 'Share ticker' field already names the asset received; it is fine as is.

cases.notes: USDe out 10 is shown exactly. feUSDEv2 in is shown by asset and recipient but not by amount, which comes from the share price.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Exactly `assets` USDe is sent from the vault to `receiver`.
feUSDEv2 shares are burned from `onBehalf`. The amount is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up, and the call has no maximum.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, the signer's share allowance from `onBehalf` is reduced by the shares burned.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly 600 USDe to <receiver>, with the amount, the recipient and the owner whose shares are used as fields.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of feUSDEv2 shares burned from the owner is not shown; the vault computes it and the call has no cap.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);`. Case 1 burned 600 feUSDEv2 from the signer, and no share amount is on screen.
findings.fix: No calldata field holds the share amount. The intent could say 'Withdraw {assets} from feUSDEv2 vault' so the signer knows which position shrinks.

cases.notes: USDe in 600 to the signer is shown exactly. Burning feUSDEv2 is implied by 'Owner' but neither the share asset nor its amount is shown.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Exactly `shares` feUSDEv2 are burned from `onBehalf`. When the signer is not the owner, the signer's share allowance is spent.
USDe equal to previewRedeem(shares), rounded down, is sent from the vault to `receiver`. The call has no minimum.
formats.shown: Redeem 10 feUSDEv2 to <receiver>, with the share amount, the recipient and the owner as fields. The asset received is never named.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never says that USDe is what the receiver gets; only the shares going out are named.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);`. Descriptor redeem interpolatedIntent is 'Redeem {#.shares} to {#.receiver}' and no field names USDe. Case 2: 9.999999999999999998 USDe arrived at the signer, and the blind reader only guessed 'likely USDe'.
findings.fix: Name the underlying, e.g. interpolatedIntent 'Redeem {#.shares} for USDe to {#.receiver}', or add a constant field 'Receive: USDe' from $.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker.

findings.title: redeem: the USDe amount received is set by the share price and has no minimum in the calldata.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. Case 2 paid 9.999999999999999998 USDe for 10 shares.
findings.fix: No calldata value to show. Naming the asset (see the warning) is the most a descriptor can do.

cases.notes: feUSDEv2 out 10 is shown exactly. USDe in is shown only as 'to receiver', with no asset and no amount; the reader guessed the asset.
